title: Lease-backed QoS smoothing and tenancy insurance for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated GPU customers need predictable throughput guarantees while permitting occasional, controlled bursts. Existing hard-quotas lead to poor utilization and customer friction; purely soft policies allow noisy neighbors to destabilize P95/P99 latencies. Proposal: implement a lease-backed QoS smoothing layer and a tenancy "insurance" credit pool that smooths short-term bursts without violating long-term throughput contracts. The approach combines: 1) Per-tenant moving-window token leases (time-limited credit allocations) that are consumed by requests and replenish at a contracted baseline rate. 2) A shared insurance fund of low-priority credits that tenants may draw when they temporarily exceed baseline—consumption from the fund is metered and can trigger throttling or billing. 3) A smoothing kernel (exponential decay) to amortize burst consumption and avoid immediate eviction. 4) Integration with autoscaler and queueing layer to convert credit pressure into scaled worker reservations, respecting SLA tiers. Implementation notes: - Token leases emitted by control-plane per tenant with attributes {baseline_qps, burst_limit, lease_ttl}. - Enforcement at runtime via scheduler-level pacing: adaptive token buckets inside the request router and soft cgroup-like pacing on GPU lanes; preferred enforcement using our runtime's per-request admission hook to avoid kernel mods. - Insurance fund implemented as a ranked pool of credits: tiered by customer priority and replenished by steady-state undersubscription and explicit allocations. - Accounting and reconciliation exported to console: per-tenant credit burn rate, fund balance, reclaimed credits, and audit trail for chargebacks. - Autoscaler integration: when median fund draw exceeds threshold for N minutes, controller will propose temporary reservation increases and surface a canary rollout; conversely, large sustained draw triggers quota enforcement and customer notifications. Observability & telemetry: new metrics (tenant_credit_balance, tenant_credit_burn_rate, fund_draw_pct, fund_replenishment_rate), trace hooks on admission decisions, and a Cost/Latency tradeoff dashboard. Rollout plan: 1) Design doc and simulation (done) 2) Prototype in dev cluster with 200 synthetic tenants (current) 3) Canary on a non-critical dedicated pool with 5 pilot customers 4) Gradual rollout with opt-in and detailed dashboard. Acceptance criteria: - No more than 5% increase in P95 latency across shielded tenants during pilot bursts - Fund prevents >90% of transient rejections for tenants with <3x baseline bursts - Accurate accounting audited by finance and visible in console UI. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: inaccurate GPU-level memory accounting prevents correct pacing. Mitigation: add a probe to runtime to measure per-request GPU memory usage; fall back to request-length heuristics. - Risk: insurance fund can be gamed by tenants. Mitigation: enforce draw caps, per-tenant decay, and billing signals; flag anomalous patterns for SRE. - Risk: coupling with autoscaler creates thrashing. Mitigation: hysteresis in controller, predictive smoothing using short-window forecasts, and conservative canary thresholds. Links: Confluence design -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Lease-backed+QoS+Smoothing; prototype repo -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/qos-smoothing; initial benchmark PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427
